baseline_models.focus_anchor: The negated predicate governs a feminine plural object, while its subject is split into ins and jann and its temporal scope is fixed by qablahum.
baseline_models.mechanism: Visible human presence and concealed spirit presence form opposed agent classes; priorness places both under one backward-looking negation. The line therefore closes earlier access across visible and hidden domains, not merely across ordinary human rivals.

activation_trace.role: Visible human presence opposed to hidden or wild beings supplies the manifest pole of the excluded agents.
Priorness or coming ahead makes the exclusion specifically about any relation occupying an earlier position.
Hidden spirit beings supply the concealed pole and expand the negation beyond visible human agency.

changed_reading.before: A generic statement that the feminine referents have had no prior sexual contact.
changed_reading.after: A recipient-relative closure of all prior access by either manifest human or concealed jinn agency.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Ins, qabl, and jann surround the negated contact predicate with perception, facing, and concealment possibilities.
baseline_models.mechanism: Perceiving brings something into awareness, facing establishes an encounter surface, and concealment withholds it. Their combination permits a perceptual reading: no earlier encounter has converted protected concealment into another agent's awareness.

activation_trace.role: Detection by sight, sense, or hearing makes entry into awareness a live dimension of contact.
Facing one thing toward another supplies the encounter interface that has not previously formed.
Covering from perception supplies the protected state that no prior encounter has opened.

changed_reading.before: The negation reports only that no bodily event occurred.
changed_reading.after: It can also report that no prior facing brought the feminine referents out of concealment and into another agent's perceptual field.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The human term can activate familiarity and intimate companionship, while qabl can activate favorable reception and jann can activate kept concealment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The denied past is relational as well as physical: no earlier familiarity, chosen companionship, or accepted reception has preempted the relation implied by qablahum. Concealment preserves an as-yet-unassigned intimacy.

activation_trace.role: Familiar comfort that removes estrangement turns contact into an established relational history.
The intimate chosen companion sharpens familiarity into a privileged personal bond.
Receiving with acceptance supplies the relational threshold that no predecessor has crossed.
Concealment preserves the bond from prior assignment rather than merely hiding a body.

changed_reading.before: The verse inventories a bodily status inherited from the past.
changed_reading.after: It preserves an unpreempted first familiarity: no earlier accepted companionship has claimed the relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent creation materials give the focus pair physical contrast: ins is associated with dry, sounding, formed matter, while jann is associated with mobile flame and kindled fire. The focus negation consequently spans two unlike modes of created agency rather than naming two interchangeable species.

activation_trace.role: Dry clay that sounds supplies the dense and audibly manifest material mode associated with the human pole.
Pottery supplies formed, bounded matter and completes the embodied side of the contrast.
A moving flame supplies the unstable, mobile material mode associated with the jann pole.
Kindled fire reinforces the subtle fiery mode opposed to formed clay.
Visible human presence anchors the material contrast back in the focus's first agent class.
Hidden spirit beings anchor the fiery contrast back in the focus's second agent class.

structural_cues: 55:14-15 places human and jann creation in adjacent, syntactically parallel clauses with contrasting materials.
The packet-listed unmapped focus predicate supplies only the shared negated-contact frame; no branch semantics are assigned to it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent creation clauses and opposed materials; I infer material contrast -> exhaustive agency contrast in 55:74. A live alternative is that the creation pair merely identifies the two audiences without changing contact semantics.

changed_reading.before: Ins and jann are a conventional exhaustive pair with no internal differentiation.
changed_reading.after: The exclusion spans both formed, manifest agency and mobile, hidden agency, making prior access impossible across contrasting created modes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The two seas can arrive face-to-face while an operative interval prevents transgressive crossing. Applied to the focus, untouchedness need not mean absolute remoteness: proximity or meeting may coexist with a maintained limit, and the negation can target boundary-violating entry.

activation_trace.role: Two things arriving face-to-face establishes real meeting rather than isolation.
The interval between two sides supplies an active relational space that separates without erasing proximity.
Crossing a limit through aggression identifies the forbidden action as breach, not mere approach.
Facing one thing toward another anchors the sea topology to the focus as a possible encounter without violation.
Protective covering supplies the maintained limit around the feminine referents.

structural_cues: 55:19-20 explicitly sequences release, meeting, an in-between barrier, and non-transgression.
The focus negates prior contact but does not itself state spatial distance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies meeting plus a non-transgressed interval; I infer that topology -> protected contact semantics in the focus. Alternatively, the sea mechanism may remain cosmological and leave 55:74 as total non-contact.

changed_reading.before: Untouchedness requires complete isolation from any encounter.
changed_reading.after: Untouchedness can persist at an interface: meeting or nearness is possible, while boundary-crossing appropriation has never occurred.

context_deltas.mechanism: The challenge to humans and jinn defines passage from one side to another as impossible except with authority or capacity. This activates a threshold model in which the focus's denied past is not generic inaccessibility but absence of any prior authorized crossing into the protected relation.

activation_trace.role: Clean passage through to the other side supplies the crossing action whose prior occurrence the focus can deny.
Sides and outer regions supply a bounded domain with an inside-to-outside threshold.
Power and jurisdiction make crossing conditional on valid capacity or authority.
Surety and undertaken responsibility give the recipient-relative relation a custodial rather than merely spatial dimension.
Protective covering makes the threshold guarded rather than naturally unreachable.

structural_cues: 55:33 directly addresses the assembly of jinn and humans and repeats the passage verb before the exception by authority.
The focus uses the same human-jinn pairing under a single negation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies paired agents, bounded sides, failed passage, and an authority exception; I infer passage rules -> relational access rules. The alternative is that sultan concerns cosmic escape only and contributes no authorization model to 55:74.

changed_reading.before: No predecessor could reach them because they were simply unavailable.
changed_reading.after: No predecessor held the capacity, jurisdiction, or entrusted claim needed to cross their protected threshold before the present recipients.

context_deltas.mechanism: Hidden precious linings coexist with harvest already near enough to take. This reverses an easy distance model: the garden can make goods near and ready while preserving an interior from prior taking. The focus can therefore mark timed non-appropriation despite availability.

activation_trace.role: A garment's lining supplies a valuable interior whose hiddenness does not depend on remoteness.
Taking produce from its growth supplies appropriation as the event that can be withheld until its proper recipient.
Nearness removes physical distance as the necessary cause of preservation.
Receiving what emerges supplies a timed handover that distinguishes readiness from prior possession.
Concealment anchors the hidden-interior analogy back in the focus.

structural_cues: 55:54 puts costly inner linings and near harvest in the same scene immediately before the first occurrence of the focus formula.
The focus's qablahum distinguishes earlier access from present readiness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden interior, taking, and nearness; I infer readiness without prior taking -> recipient-timed access in the focus. Alternatively, the furnishing and fruit images may describe abundance without governing personal relation.

changed_reading.before: Preservation is explained by seclusion and distance.
changed_reading.after: The referents may be near and ready yet never previously appropriated; firstness is controlled by timing and recipient, not by remoteness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The first occurrence of the focus formula follows attention confined to a limit, while the second follows figures confined within tents. Gaze and dwelling create nested perceptual and spatial boundaries, strengthening the baseline in which prior contact includes unauthorized seeing, orientation, and entry rather than only a bodily act.

activation_trace.role: Confining something to a limit supplies deliberate restriction rather than accidental absence.
The glance and visual faculty specify perception as one restricted channel of relation.
An enclosed building turns restriction into a spatial architecture immediately before the focus.
Tent and settled dwelling supply the inhabitable enclosure within which access is bounded.
Perception by sight or sense anchors restricted gaze as a genuine dimension of the focus's contact.
Concealment joins the gaze and dwelling limits into one protected perceptual-spatial state.

structural_cues: 55:56 adds restricted gaze before repeating the full 55:74 predicate.
55:72 places confinement in tents immediately before 55:74.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies restricted attention, enclosure, and two placements of the same predicate; I infer nested boundaries -> expanded contact semantics. A live alternative keeps gaze and tents as separate descriptions while the focus remains narrowly sexual.

changed_reading.before: Untouchedness is a single bodily property.
changed_reading.after: It is a nested access condition: no prior agent has entered the protected circuits of gaze, perceptual encounter, dwelling, or body.

context_deltas.mechanism: Good action answered by good supplies a reciprocal arrow between prior conduct and garden reception. Within that frame, qablahum can make the denied prior relation part of a fitting return to the present recipients, not an abstract quality detached from them.

activation_trace.role: Answering an act with its recompense supplies the explicit reciprocal mechanism.
Doing what is good supplies both sides of the act-for-answer correspondence.
Favorable reception turns qablahum toward a relation fitted to and received by the current recipients.
Chosen intimate companionship supplies the personal good reserved within the reciprocal frame.

structural_cues: 55:60 states good-for-good between the two garden descriptions.
The suffix in qablahum makes the focus explicitly relative to present recipients rather than merely absolute.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit recompense equation and recipient-relative priorness; I infer good conduct -> fitting unpreempted reception. Alternatively, 55:60 may summarize reward generally without assigning a causal arrow to this particular relation.

changed_reading.before: The denied past is an intrinsic status with no relation to the garden recipients' history.
changed_reading.after: The unpreempted bond can function as reciprocal good: a first accepted companionship fitted to those who now receive it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same prior-contact formula appears once in each garden sequence, while dun marks another or lower pair and jannah activates tree-covering from the same root as jann. Repetition converts the line from a one-off biography into a boundary condition invariant across distinct covered garden registers.

activation_trace.role: The same priorness branch in the first occurrence establishes exact temporal parallelism with the focus.
Otherness distinguishes a second garden register without dissolving its parallel relation to the first.
A tree-covered garden supplies the sheltered habitat and activates covering within the same root as the focus's jann.
Focus priorness completes the repeated temporal condition in the second garden register.
The hidden-being branch preserves the literal agent while resonating with the garden's covering branch.

structural_cues: 55:56 and 55:74 repeat the same full clause in corresponding positions of two garden sequences.
55:62 introduces another or lower pair of gardens between those occurrences.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact repetition, paired garden blocks, and same-root covering resonance; I infer repetition -> invariant access rule across registers. The alternative is formal parallelism with no added mechanism beyond emphasis.

changed_reading.before: The focus reports an isolated personal fact about one group.
changed_reading.after: It restates a garden-wide invariant: across distinct sheltered registers, the promised relation arrives without a predecessor.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate refrain asks the paired addressees whether they deny their Lord's favors. Its placement categorizes the focus claim as an ala to be recognized within divine nurture and completion. The line shifts from detached description to an addressed benefit whose protected firstness demands acknowledgment.

activation_trace.role: Favors or blessings explicitly class the preceding focus statement as benefaction.
Cultivation, repair, and completion frame the protected relation as deliberately brought to readiness.
Contradicting truth makes recognition or denial the audience's required response to the benefit.
Favorable reception links the recipients' first relation to the refrain's demand that they receive the favor as true.

structural_cues: 55:75 immediately follows the focus with the surah's repeated dual-address refrain.
The refrain repeatedly closes both gift and warning units, so its local scope can classify rather than merely decorate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate adjacency and repeated favor-denial framing; I infer the refrain scopes backward -> 55:74 is presented as benefaction. A live alternative is that the refrain closes the whole garden bundle without classifying each preceding detail separately.

changed_reading.before: The focus is a neutral status claim available for detached inspection.
changed_reading.after: It is an addressed favor: protected, recipient-specific firstness is something the paired audience must recognize rather than reduce to inventory.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the residue branch of the garden's gushing-water root rather than its obvious water branch. It remains anchored in the focus's negated prior contact, perceptibility, and priorness; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for evidentiary trace, not as a lexical gloss of the focus predicate.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The negated contact predicate can be tested not only as an event but by whether any perceivable remainder from an earlier event exists.

activation_trace.role: A daub whose trace remains supplies the material counterfactual: prior contact would leave residue.
Perceiving or detecting supplies the evidentiary act by which a remainder would become known.
Priorness locates the hypothetical residue in an earlier relation rather than the present one.

changed_reading.before: The verse denies a past act.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also denies the material or perceptual residue by which any past claimant could be detected.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the little human image seen in the pupil and combines it with eye and facing cues. It remains visibly anchored in focus ins, focus qabl, and the gaze sequence at 55:56/72; downstream prose should call it an optical analogy for first encounter, never claim that insan literally means pupil-image here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Focus ins can carry an eye-image branch, while focus qabl can carry face-to-face orientation and the surrounding descriptions foreground gaze and eyes.

activation_trace.role: The glance and visual faculty make the eye an explicit local interface of relation.
Marked eye contrast keeps the optical register active immediately before the focus.
The human-like image in the pupil supplies the strange but concrete model of another person entering one's visual field.
Face-to-face orientation turns the pupil image into a mutual encounter rather than unilateral inspection.
Concealment supplies the previously unoccupied visual state that first facing would open.

changed_reading.before: The denied history concerns only bodily possession.
changed_reading.after: As an optical analogy, no predecessor has occupied the scene of mutual recognition; the promised encounter is also a first face and first image.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates fresh-beginning branches under words whose surface senses here are priorness and jann. It remains anchored through two independent focus-root branches converging on newness plus the intimate-companion branch; downstream prose should render it as abductive resonance, not substitute those branch senses into the sentence.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Within the focus inventories, qabl and jann independently contain fresh-beginning branches, while ins contains an intimate-companion branch.

activation_trace.role: A fresh, unprepared beginning converts absence of predecessors into positive inaugural immediacy.
Freshness at a thing's beginning independently reinforces the inaugural rather than merely privative reading.
The intimate chosen companion gives the fresh beginning a relational object and keeps it anchored in the focus.

changed_reading.before: The verse is privative: it says only that an earlier relation is absent.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the doubled newness branches make that absence generative: the intimate relation begins without inherited script, residue, or predecessor.

strongest_changes: The sea-barrier sequence replaces simple isolation with meeting that does not become transgressive crossing.
The passage-and-authority sequence recasts untouchedness as guarded, recipient-relative access rather than natural unavailability.
The exact 55:56/55:74 repetition makes the clause a boundary invariant across two garden registers, while gaze and tent cues widen contact into perceptual and spatial access.
The immediate refrain reclassifies protected firstness as an addressed benefaction to be recognized.
summary.what_was_special: The visible-human/hidden-jann pair activated material, optical, legal, ecological, and relational mechanisms at once. The most productive tension is that nearness, meeting, and readiness coexist with non-appropriation; no single reading should erase the others.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet supplies no branch inventory for the focus predicate, so the exact kind of contact remains a structural anchor rather than a branch-resolved semantic decision.
The context supports a recipient-relative reading of qablahum but does not by itself settle every pronoun antecedent or prove that reciprocity causes the reserved relation.
The residue, pupil-image, surety, and fresh-beginning activations are useful abductive resonances but must not be rendered as direct lexical substitutions.
